claim: Creolimax fragrantissima is a relative of animals that undergoes coenocytic development.
source: To address this question, we investigated transcriptional dynamics in the ichthyosporean Creolimax fragrantissima, a relative of animals that undergoes coenocytic development.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a description of the study organism.

claim: Creolimax utilizes dynamic regulation of alternative splicing in a cell-type specific manner.
source: We find that Creolimax utilizes dynamic regulation of alternative splicing, long inter-genic non-coding RNAs and co-regulated gene modules associated with animal multicellularity in a cell-type specific manner.
evidence: Directly stated finding in the abstract based on the study's results.

claim: Creolimax utilizes long inter-genic non-coding RNAs in a cell-type specific manner.
source: We find that Creolimax utilizes dynamic regulation of alternative splicing, long inter-genic non-coding RNAs and co-regulated gene modules associated with animal multicellularity in a cell-type specific manner.
evidence: Directly stated finding in the abstract based on the study's results.

claim: Creolimax utilizes co-regulated gene modules associated with animal multicellularity in a cell-type specific manner.
source: We find that Creolimax utilizes dynamic regulation of alternative splicing, long inter-genic non-coding RNAs and co-regulated gene modules associated with animal multicellularity in a cell-type specific manner.
evidence: Directly stated finding in the abstract based on the study's results.

claim: The different cell types of ichthyosporeans, filastereans and choanoflagellates are the product of lineage-specific innovations.
source: Moreover, our study suggests that the different cell types of the three closest animal relatives (ichthyosporeans, filastereans and choanoflagellates) are the product of lineage-specific innovations.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the study's comparative analysis.

claim: A proteomic survey of the Creolimax secretome reveals adaptations to a fungal-like lifestyle.
source: Additionally, a proteomic survey of the secretome reveals adaptations to a fungal-like lifestyle.
evidence: Directly stated finding in the abstract based on proteomic data.

claim: The last unicellular ancestor of animals was already capable of elaborate specification of cell types.
source: In summary, the diversity of cell types among protistan relatives of animals and their complex genome regulation demonstrates that the last unicellular ancestor of animals was already capable of elaborate specification of cell types.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the study's findings about genome regulation complexity.

claim: The development of complex multicellularity is dependent upon differential genome regulation.
source: As the development of complex multicellularity is dependent upon differential genome regulation, the evolutionary onset of animal multicellularity must likewise have involved the appearance of differential genome regulatory capacities leading to distinct cell types.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Many genes involved in the control of animal development and cell type identity pre-date animal origins.
source: Many of the genes involved in the control of animal development and cell type identity, including signaling pathways and transcription factors (TFs), pre-date animal origins (Sebe-Pedros et al., 2011; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2012; Suga et al., 2012; Richter and King, 2013).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: Genes involved in animal development are present in the genomes of protistan relatives of animals.
source: As these genes are known to be present in the genomes of the protistan relatives of animals, the unicellular holozoans (King et al., 2008; Suga et al., 2013; Fairclough et al., 2013), the evolution of complex multicellularity, with cell type-specific transcriptional programs, must have involved changes in gene regulation.
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: Three distinct developmental modes that lead to transient simple multicellular forms have been described in the protistan relatives of animals.
source: Three distinct developmental modes that lead to transient simple multicellular forms have been described in the protistan relatives of animals (Figure 1) (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013; Suga and Ruiz-Trillo, 2013; Dayel et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations and reference to Figure 1.

claim: Colonial clonal development in Salpingoeca rosetta involves differential regulation of a few multicellularity-related genes.
source: Colonial clonal development has been shown to involve differential regulation of a few multicellularity-related genes in the choanoflagellate Salpingoeca rosetta (Fairclough et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with supporting citation to previous research.

claim: Capsaspora owczarzaki exhibits up-regulation of adhesion-related genes in its aggregative stage.
source: On the other hand, the filasterean amoeba Capsaspora owczarzaki exhibits up-regulation of adhesion-related genes in its aggregative stage (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with supporting citation to previous research.

claim: There has been no molecular characterization of coenocytic development prior to this study.
source: To date, however, there has been no molecular characterization of coenocytic development, a third and completely distinct mode of development observed in the ichthyosporeans.
evidence: Stated as a gap in knowledge that this study addresses.

claim: Ichthyosporeans are the earliest branching holozoan lineage.
source: Ichthyosporeans are the earliest branching holozoan lineage (Torruella et al., 2012; Paps et al., 2013; Torruella et al., 2015), and coenocytic development is a shared feature within the group (Glockling et al., 2013; Mendoza et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: Coenocytic development is a shared feature within the ichthyosporean group.
source: Ichthyosporeans are the earliest branching holozoan lineage (Torruella et al., 2012; Paps et al., 2013; Torruella et al., 2015), and coenocytic development is a shared feature within the group (Glockling et al., 2013; Mendoza et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: Coenocytic development comprises a growth stage in which nuclei divide synchronously within a common cytoplasm before undergoing cellularization.
source: This developmental mode comprises a growth stage in which nuclei divide synchronously within a common cytoplasm before undergoing cellularization, followed by release of motile ameboid zoospores (Suga and Ruiz-Trillo, 2013; Marshall et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: The amoeboid stage of Creolimax is mono-nucleated, non-dividing, and motile.
source: These stages have distinct physiological and structural characteristics, the amoeboid stage is mono-nucleated, non-diving, and motile (Figure 1B), while the multinucleate stage has a cell wall, a big central vacuole, and does not move (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated directly with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The multinucleate stage of Creolimax has a cell wall, a big central vacuole, and does not move.
source: These stages have distinct physiological and structural characteristics, the amoeboid stage is mono-nucleated, non-diving, and motile (Figure 1B), while the multinucleate stage has a cell wall, a big central vacuole, and does not move (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated directly with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Coenocytic development and multinucleate cell types are found in some animal lineages, such as in Drosophila syncytial blastoderm.
source: Despite being quite distinct from canonic animal development, coenocytic development and multinucleate cell types are found in some animal lineages, such as in Drosophila syncytial blastoderm (Suga and Ruiz-Trillo, 2013).
evidence: Stated with supporting citation to previous research.

claim: The Creolimax draft genome is 45 Mb in size.
source: As a reference genome for mapping RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data, we assembled the 45 Mb draft genome of Creolimax from a combination of 454 reads and mate-paired end Illumina reads corresponding to a 75× coverage.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome assembly.

claim: The Creolimax draft assembly comprises 82 scaffolds, with an N50 of 1.5 Mb.
source: The draft assembly comprises 82 scaffolds, with an N50 of 1.5 Mb (see Materials and methods).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome assembly.

claim: The Creolimax genome is twice as large as that of Capsaspora.
source: The genome is twice as large as that of Capsaspora but in line with sequenced choanoflagellate genomes.
evidence: Stated as a comparative observation.

claim: 8695 genes were annotated in the Creolimax genome.
source: We annotated 8695 genes, 92% of which are supported by transcriptional evidence.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome annotation.

claim: 92% of annotated Creolimax genes are supported by transcriptional evidence.
source: We annotated 8695 genes, 92% of which are supported by transcriptional evidence.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome annotation.

claim: Functional information was obtained for 78% of the predicted protein coding genes in Creolimax.
source: A diverse array of annotation pipelines rendered functional information on 78% of the predicted protein coding genes (see Material and methods).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of functional annotation.

claim: Many Creolimax genes belong to gene families involved in multicellularity and development in animals.
source: Among those genes, many belong to gene families involved in multicellularity and development in animals, such as TFs and signaling pathways, as previously reported in targeted gene family analysis (Suga et al., 2014; de Mendoza et al., 2013; de Mendoza et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated with supporting citations to previous research.

claim: The amoeboid and multinucleate stages of Creolimax showed distinct transcriptional profiles, consistent among replicates.
source: The amoeboid and the multinucleate stage showed distinct transcriptional profiles, consistent among replicates (Figure 2A), from which we identified 956 genes as significantly differentially expressed.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of RNA-seq analysis with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: 956 genes were identified as significantly differentially expressed between the amoeboid and multinucleate stages.
source: The amoeboid and the multinucleate stage showed distinct transcriptional profiles, consistent among replicates (Figure 2A), from which we identified 956 genes as significantly differentially expressed.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential expression analysis.

claim: The multinucleate stage shows up-regulation of genes associated with cell growth, including ribosome, translation, DNA replication, amino acid and RNA metabolism activities.
source: Functional enrichment analyses of Gene Ontologies (GOs) and PFAM domains (p<0.01, Fisher's exact test) revealed that the multinucleate stage shows up-regulation of genes associated with cell growth, including ribosome, translation, DNA replication, amino acid and RNA metabolism activities (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of functional enrichment analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The amoeboid stage shows enrichment for signaling activities (GTPases and kinases) and up-regulation of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Conversely, in the amoeboid stage, we found enrichment for signaling activities (GTPases and kinases) and an up-regulation of the actin cytoskeleton, most likely involved in the motile behavior of the amoeba (see raw GOs in Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of functional enrichment analysis.

claim: Single-celled amoebas showed up-regulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) adhesion, including the up-regulation of the integrin pathway components.
source: Strikingly, single-celled amoebas also showed up-regulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) adhesion, including the up-regulation of the integrin pathway components.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of functional enrichment analysis.

claim: TF expression is higher in the amoeboid stage compared to the multinucleate stage.
source: Contrary to our expectation, the comparison revealed that TF expression is higher in the amoeboid stage (p<0.05, Wilcoxon signed rank test, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of statistical comparison with reference to figure.

claim: 127 putative TFs were found in the Creolimax genome.
source: Among the 127 putative TFs found in the genome, only 5 are significantly up-regulated in the multinucleate stage.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome annotation and expression analysis.

claim: Only 5 TFs are significantly up-regulated in the multinucleate stage.
source: Among the 127 putative TFs found in the genome, only 5 are significantly up-regulated in the multinucleate stage.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential expression analysis.

claim: 11 TFs are significantly up-regulated in the amoeboid stage, including T-box, Runx and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis TFs.
source: In the amoeboid stage, we found significant up-regulation of 11 TFs, including T-box, Runx and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis TFs, and TF classes that have important roles in animal development (Sebe-Pedros et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential expression analysis with citation.

claim: Unlike in animal development, the multinucleate stage of Creolimax is not characterized by a tight regulation of adhesive, signaling, and TF activities.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that, unlike in animal development, the multinucleate stage of Creolimax is not characterized by a tight regulation of adhesive, signaling, and TF activities.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the expression analysis data.

claim: The Creolimax genome has an average of 6.5 introns per gene.
source: To evaluate the extent to which alternative splicing expands transcriptome complexity in the intron-rich genome of Creolimax (6.5 introns per gene), we undertook a comprehensive analysis of intron retention and exon skipping (ES) events, and quantified their inclusion levels using previously developed pipelines (Braunschweig et al., 2014; Irimia et al., 2014) (see Material and methods).
evidence: Stated directly as a characteristic of the genome.

claim: 3927 intron-retention events were observed that affected 2172 genes in Creolimax.
source: We observed 3927 intron-retention events that affected 2172 genes.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of alternative splicing analysis.

claim: 211 genes were affected by exon skipping in Creolimax.
source: In contrast, we found only 211 genes affected by ES.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of alternative splicing analysis.

claim: Creolimax has a two-fold higher intron density compared to Capsaspora.
source: Despite having a two-fold higher intron density and longer introns compared to Capsaspora, both holozoan species show comparable alternative splicing profiles that are highly dominated by intron retention (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a comparative observation with citation.

claim: Both Creolimax and Capsaspora show alternative splicing profiles that are highly dominated by intron retention.
source: Despite having a two-fold higher intron density and longer introns compared to Capsaspora, both holozoan species show comparable alternative splicing profiles that are highly dominated by intron retention (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a comparative observation with citation.

claim: ES-dominated alternative splicing is a unique feature of animal transcriptomes.
source: This provides further support for the hypothesis that ES-dominated alternative splicing is a unique feature of animal transcriptomes (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013; Mcguire et al., 2008; Irimia and Roy, 2014).
evidence: Stated as a hypothesis supported by the data with citations.

claim: 865 introns with differential retention between stages were found in Creolimax.
source: We found 865 introns with differential retention between stages (differential percent intron retention (ΔPIR) >15), the majority of which were more retained in the amoeboid stage (Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential alternative splicing analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The majority of differentially retained introns were more retained in the amoeboid stage.
source: We found 865 introns with differential retention between stages (differential percent intron retention (ΔPIR) >15), the majority of which were more retained in the amoeboid stage (Figure 3A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential alternative splicing analysis with reference to figure.

claim: RT-PCR assays confirmed differential retention for all 10 tested introns.
source: Reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assays confirmed differential retention for all 10 tested introns (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of experimental validation with reference to figures.

claim: Genes with amoeboid-specific intron retention showed enrichment in spindle pole formation and other mitosis-related activities.
source: GO enrichment analysis of genes with amoeboid-specific intron retention revealed enrichment in spindle pole formation and other mitosis-related activities (Figure 3C), supporting an active role of IR in down-regulating these functions in this stage.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of GO enrichment analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Genes with amoeboid-specific intron retention showed significantly lower steady-state mRNA levels compared to the multinucleate stage.
source: Indeed, consistent with recent reports in vertebrates (Braunschweig et al., 2014), genes with amoeboid-specific intron retention showed significantly lower steady-state mRNA levels compared to the multinucleate stage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C; p<0.0001, Wilcoxon signed rank test; the converse was true for genes with multinucleate-specific intron retention).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of expression analysis with statistical test and reference to figure.

claim: Intron retention is a conserved mechanism for reducing transcript levels in pathway-specific genes from unicellular holozoans to vertebrates.
source: Therefore, intron retention is a conserved mechanism for reducing transcript levels in pathway-specific genes from unicellular holozoans to vertebrates.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the data and comparison with vertebrates.

claim: 63 exons with differential inclusion levels across stages were found in Creolimax.
source: In the case of ES, we found 63 exons with differential inclusion levels across stages (Figure 3B).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential alternative splicing analysis with reference to figure.

claim: RT-PCR assays validated the differential inclusion for all 12 tested exon skipping cases.
source: RT-PCR assays were used to validate the differential inclusion for all 12 tested cases (Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of experimental validation with reference to figures.

claim: Only a minority of differentially skipped exons keep the reading frame upon skipping.
source: Only a minority of these exons (Torruella et al., 2015) keep the reading frame upon skipping, and only two of these overlapped with functional Pfam domains, suggesting that, similar to intron retention, ES in Creolimax predominantly contributed to functionally down-regulating specific genes.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of analysis with inference about function.

claim: 692 putative lincRNA loci were identified in Creolimax.
source: Restricting our search to transcripts that did not overlap with protein-coding genes, known as long-intergenic RNAs (lincRNAs ), we identified 692 putative lincRNA loci in Creolimax.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of lincRNA identification pipeline.

claim: lincRNAs in Creolimax were shorter in length compared to protein-coding transcripts.
source: In comparison to protein-coding transcripts, lincRNAs in Creolimax were shorter in length, harbored fewer exons, had longer exons, and had a lower GC content (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of comparative analysis with reference to figure.

claim: lincRNAs in Creolimax harbored fewer exons compared to protein-coding transcripts.
source: In comparison to protein-coding transcripts, lincRNAs in Creolimax were shorter in length, harbored fewer exons, had longer exons, and had a lower GC content (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of comparative analysis with reference to figure.

claim: lincRNAs in Creolimax had longer exons compared to protein-coding transcripts.
source: In comparison to protein-coding transcripts, lincRNAs in Creolimax were shorter in length, harbored fewer exons, had longer exons, and had a lower GC content (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of comparative analysis with reference to figure.

claim: lincRNAs in Creolimax had a lower GC content compared to protein-coding transcripts.
source: In comparison to protein-coding transcripts, lincRNAs in Creolimax were shorter in length, harbored fewer exons, had longer exons, and had a lower GC content (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of comparative analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Overall transcription levels of lincRNAs were significantly lower than those of protein-coding genes in Creolimax.
source: Moreover, overall transcription levels of lincRNAs were significantly lower than those of protein-coding genes (p<0.01, Wilcoxon rank sum test).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of statistical comparison.

claim: The characteristics of Creolimax lincRNAs have been reported for animal lincRNAs.
source: Interestingly, all those characteristics have been reported for animal lincRNAs (Hezroni et al., 2015; Pauli et al., 2012; Gaiti et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citations to previous research.

claim: 23.6% of TFs in Creolimax had at least one neighboring lincRNA, a significant enrichment compared to the rest of the genome.
source: However, when we analyzed the vicinity of all the TFs, we found that 23.6% had at least one neighboring lincRNA, a significant enrichment compared to the rest of the genome (14.5%, p=0.0007, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of statistical analysis.

claim: No putative homologs of Creolimax lincRNAs were found in the transcriptomes of closely related species and other unicellular holozoans.
source: Next, we searched for putative homologs of the lincRNAs in the transcriptomes of closely related species and other unicellular holozoans, but we did not retrieve any positive hits.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of homology search.

claim: Rapid evolutionary sequence turnover of lincRNAs has been described for animals.
source: This pattern of rapid evolutionary sequence turnover of lincRNAs has also been described for animals (Gaiti et al., 2015; Kapusta and Feschotte, 2014), where homology detection based on sequence similarity is restricted to short evolutionary distances.
evidence: Stated with citations to previous research.

claim: 51 lincRNA loci were differentially expressed between the amoeba and the multinucleate stage in Creolimax.
source: In Creolimax we detected 51 lincRNA loci that were differentially expressed between the amoeba and the multinucleate stage (Figure 4).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential expression analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Only 7% of the total detected lincRNAs are differentially expressed in Creolimax, compared to 10% of coding genes.
source: Overall, only 7% of the total detected lincRNAs are differentially expressed, compared to 10% of coding genes (p=0.0059, Fisher's exact test).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of statistical comparison.

claim: In stark contrast to animals, the lincRNAs in Creolimax appear to be less cell type-specific than coding genes.
source: Thus, in stark contrast to animals, the lincRNAs in Creolimax appear to be less cell type-specific than coding genes.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the differential expression data.

claim: Head-to-head orientation of lincRNAs was significantly over-represented in the Creolimax genome.
source: Head-to-head orientation was significantly over-represented in the genome (485/692, 70% of the total vs the 50% expected by chance, p<3.6e-14, χ2 test).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of statistical analysis.

claim: 80% of differentially regulated lincRNAs are in head-to-tail orientation or display uncoupled transcriptional profiles in relation to their neighbor genes.
source: Moreover, 80% of differentially regulated lincRNAs are in head-to-tail orientation or display uncoupled transcriptional profiles in relation to their neighbor genes (p<0.05 Pearson's correlation coefficient).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis.

claim: 132 lincRNA loci in Creolimax have two or more exons.
source: Although the majority of lincRNAs have a single exon, 132 (19.1%) loci have two or more exons.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of structural analysis.

claim: 183 intron-retention events were detected among multi-exon lincRNA transcripts in Creolimax.
source: Among those multi-exon transcripts, we detected 183 intron-retention events (Figure 4E).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of alternative splicing analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Eight intron retention events in lincRNAs differed between samples, suggesting differential regulation.
source: Of these, eight events differed between samples (PIR>15), suggesting differential regulation of lincRNAs also at the level of splicing.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of differential alternative splicing analysis with inference.

claim: Both transcriptional regulation and alternative splicing may play a role in the active regulation of lincRNAs in Creolimax.
source: Therefore, both transcriptional regulation and alternative splicing may play a role in the active regulation of lincRNAs in Creolimax.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the data.

claim: Hierarchical clustering and neighbor-joining tree reconstructions showed species-specific clustering for the different stages of unicellular holozoans.
source: Both approaches showed consistent trees with species-specific clustering for the different stages.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Creolimax multinucleate stage and Capsaspora cystic stage are the most dissimilar among all samples.
source: Direct cell type comparisons between species revealed that Creolimax multinucleate stage and Capsaspora cystic stage are the most dissimilar among all samples, whereas the amoeboid stage in Creolimax has a stronger correlation with the filopodial and aggregative stages of Capsaspora (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The amoeboid stage in Creolimax has a stronger correlation with the filopodial and aggregative stages of Capsaspora.
source: Direct cell type comparisons between species revealed that Creolimax multinucleate stage and Capsaspora cystic stage are the most dissimilar among all samples, whereas the amoeboid stage in Creolimax has a stronger correlation with the filopodial and aggregative stages of Capsaspora (Figure 5A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure.

claim: PC2 grouped the multinucleate stages of Creolimax with the aggregative and the filopodial stages of Capsaspora, explained by genes involved in DNA replication and spliceosomal activities.
source: PC2 grouped the multinucleate stages of Creolimax with the aggregative and the filopodial stages of Capsaspora. This grouping was explained by top-loading genes involved in DNA replication and spliceosomal activities (Figure 5D), a pattern consistent with the down-regulation of mitotic activity and cell growth in the Capsaspora cystic stage (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of PCA analysis with reference to figure and citation.

claim: PC3 grouped the amoeboid stage of Creolimax and the filopodial and aggregative stages of Capsaspora, loaded with genes involved in the integrin adhesome and amoeboid actin-based motility and signaling activities.
source: On the other hand, PC3 grouped the amoeboid stage of Creolimax and the filopodial and aggregative stages of Capsaspora. PC3 was loaded with genes involved in the integrin adhesome and amoeboid actin-based motility and signaling activities (Figure 5D).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of PCA analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Human cell types with a higher positive correlation with the multinucleate stage were those with high proliferation rates, including embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells and transformed cell lines.
source: The human cell types with a higher positive correlation with the multinucleate stage were those with high proliferation rates, including embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells and transformed cell lines (293T, HeLA, K562) (Figure 6B).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure.

claim: PC2 distinguished between highly proliferative cell types and the rest in both Creolimax and human.
source: Similar patterns were obtained using PCA on the normalized steady-state transcriptional levels from both species. PC1 explained most of the variability due to species-specific transcriptomic profiles, whereas PC2 distinguished between highly proliferative cell types and the rest in both species (Figure 6C).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of PCA analysis with reference to figure.

claim: GO enrichment analysis of the top 125 genes that most contributed to PC2 showed highly significant enrichment for genes involved in genome replication and proliferation.
source: Consistent with this observation, GO enrichment analysis of the top 125 genes that most contributed to PC2 showed highly significant enrichment for genes involved in genome replication and proliferation (Figure 6D).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of GO enrichment analysis with reference to figure.

claim: A signal from the evolutionarily conserved machinery for cell proliferation in eukaryotes can be detected from direct expression pattern comparisons between the multinucleate stage of Creolimax and highly proliferative human cell types.
source: These results suggest that a signal from the evolutionarily conserved machinery for cell proliferation in eukaryotes (Harashima et al., 2013; Cross et al., 2011) can be detected from direct expression pattern comparisons between the multinucleate stage of Creolimax and highly proliferative human cell types.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the data with citations.

claim: Creolimax has a nearly complete repertoire of the integrin adhesome components.
source: In the case of Creolimax, we found a nearly complete repertoire of the integrin adhesome components (Figure 7D), and most of them are significantly up-regulated in the amoeboid stage (Figure 7A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Most integrin adhesome components are significantly up-regulated in the amoeboid stage of Creolimax.
source: In the case of Creolimax, we found a nearly complete repertoire of the integrin adhesome components (Figure 7D), and most of them are significantly up-regulated in the amoeboid stage (Figure 7A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of expression analysis with reference to figure.

claim: A remarkable co-regulation among all of the integrin adhesome components was observed in Creolimax, with the exception of the Src tyrosine kinase.
source: In the case of Creolimax, we observed a remarkable co-regulation among all of the components. The only exception is the Src tyrosine kinase (Figure 7A), suggesting that tyrosine kinase signaling is not connected to the integrin signaling pathway in Creolimax, consistent with the absence of a focal adhesion kinase in the ichthyosporean lineage (Suga et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure and citation.

claim: A more complex pattern of co-regulation was identified in Capsaspora, grouped in two submodules associated with specific paralogs of both alpha and beta integrins.
source: In the filasterean Capsaspora, we identified a more complex pattern of co-regulation, grouped in two submodules that are associated with specific paralogs of both alpha and beta integrins (Figure 7B).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure.

claim: No co-regulation among the few conserved integrin adhesome components was detected in the choanoflagellate Salpingoeca.
source: In contrast, we did not detect any co-regulation among the few conserved integrin adhesome components in the choanoflagellate Salpingoeca (Figure 7C), suggesting that gene loss in the choanoflagellate lineage was accompanied by dismantling of this ancient co-regulatory module.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure and inference.

claim: No laminin-containing genes were found in Creolimax.
source: However, despite showing a co-regulated integrin adhesome, we did not find any laminin-containing genes in Creolimax (Figure 7E).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The only ECM-related domains found in the Creolimax genome were fibronectins, but those are fused to metabolic domains unrelated to the ECM and none had a secretion signal peptide.
source: The only ECM-related domains that we found in the genome were fibronectins, but those are fused to metabolic domains unrelated to the ECM and none had a secretion signal peptide (Figure 7F).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome analysis with reference to figure.

claim: It seems unlikely that integrins are involved in adhesion to an endogenous animal-like ECM in Creolimax.
source: Therefore, it seems unlikely that integrins are involved in adhesion to an endogenous animal-like ECM in Creolimax.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the absence of ECM components.

claim: Strong positive co-regulation of a core set of filopodial machinery components was observed in all unicellular holozoans.
source: Next, we investigated the filopodial machinery (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2013). We observed strong positive co-regulation of a core set of components in all unicellular holozoans (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), consistent with the use of an ancestral cellular machinery for filopodial formation.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure and inference.

claim: No single co-regulated module was observed in any unicellular species for genes involved in animal neuronal pre-synaptic and post-synaptic processes.
source: In stark contrast to the situation for cell replication machinery, we did not observe a single co-regulated module in any unicellular species for genes involved in animal neuronal pre-synaptic and post-synaptic processes, including most pairs of genes that are known to directly interact in animals (with the exception of syntaxin, synaptobrevin, and synaptogryin, which are involved in secretory vesicle formation (Burkhardt et al., 2011); Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of correlation analysis with reference to figure and citation.

claim: Some molecular complexes directly involved in cell morphology and behavior already formed co-regulated gene modules in unicellular holozoans.
source: Thus, our results suggest that some molecular complexes directly involved in cell morphology and behavior already formed co-regulated gene modules in unicellular holozoans, whereas other complexes involved in unique animal cell types were assembled later, despite having conserved orthologs.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the co-regulation analysis.

claim: Ichthyosporeans were once thought to be fungi based on their lifestyle and morphology.
source: Ichthyosporeans are an interesting case of convergent evolution of fungal-like traits; in fact, they were once thought to be fungi based on their lifestyle and morphology (Glockling et al., 2013; Mendoza et al., 2002).
evidence: Stated with citations to previous research.

claim: Both ichthyosporeans and fungi have a cell wall, similar parasitic lifestyles, and a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode.
source: For instance, both groups have a cell wall, similar parasitic lifestyles, and a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode, unlike any of the other holozoan lineages (Figure 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a comparison with reference to figure.

claim: 91 proteins were identified in the in vivo secretome sample using high-throughput proteomics.
source: To characterize the secretome, we performed a combination of in vivo and in silico approaches. First, using high-throughput proteomics of an in vivo secretome sample in culture conditions, we identified 91 proteins.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of proteomic analysis.

claim: 453 proteins are predicted to be secreted using an in silico approach.
source: Next, we applied an in silico approach to predict 453 proteins that are likely to be secreted (see Material and methods).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of computational prediction.

claim: Only 48 proteins were common to both the in vivo and in silico secretome datasets.
source: Interestingly, only 48 proteins were common to both datasets, indicating that proteins without a canonical signal peptide or with additional transmembrane domains could also be found in the in vivo secretome (Figure 8A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of dataset comparison with reference to figure.

claim: Peptides corresponding to the extracellular region of both alpha and beta integrins were found in the in vivo secretome.
source: For instance, we found peptides corresponding to the extracellular region of both alpha and beta integrins.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of proteomic analysis.

claim: Both secretome datasets were highly enriched in peptidase and proteolytic activities.
source: Both secretome datasets were highly enriched in peptidase and proteolytic activities (Figure 8B), whereas only the in silico dataset showed further enrichments in other catabolic functions such as lipase and hydrolase activities.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of functional enrichment analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The proteolytic activity of the Creolimax secretome does not seem to be related to modifying the endogenous ECM, but possibly to the adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode.
source: Thus, the proteolytic activity of the Creolimax secretome does not seem to be related to modifying the endogenous ECM, but possibly to the adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the secretome analysis.

claim: The enrichment in proteolytic activities observed in the secretome strongly suggests that proteins and peptides are the main food source of Creolimax, at least under culture conditions.
source: Osmotrophic lifestyles are characterized by the external digestion of complex polymers (Talbot, 2013). Therefore, the enrichment in proteolytic activities observed in the secretome strongly suggests that proteins and peptides are the main food source of Creolimax, at least under culture conditions.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the secretome analysis with citation.

claim: 38 genes with four distinct Pfam domains are predicted to be involved in the amino acid and oligopeptide transporter activity in Creolimax.
source: Consistent with this requirement, we found 38 genes with four distinct Pfam domains (PF00324, PF01490, PF03169 and PF00854) that are predicted to be involved in the amino acid and oligopeptide transporter activity.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome analysis.

claim: Trypsins are the most-abundant gene family in Creolimax secretome, with 15 proteins in the in vivo proteomic dataset out of the 31 genes found in the genome.
source: The most-abundant gene family in Creolimax secretome was the trypsins (15 proteins in the in vivo proteomic dataset out of the 31 genes found in the genome).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of proteomic and genome analysis.

claim: Independent expansions of trypsins were found in other osmotrophic lineages.
source: To further complement these observations, we profiled a wide range of eukaryotes and found independent expansions of trypsins in other osmotrophic lineages (Figure 9A).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of comparative genomic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Most Creolimax trypsins are the product of rapid lineage-specific gene duplications.
source: Phylogenetic analyses of Creolimax trypsins (Figure 9B) revealed that most are the product of rapid lineage-specific gene duplications, a common source of molecular adaptation (Kondrashov, 2012).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis with reference to figure and citation.

claim: Very distinct patterns of transcript and protein abundance were found across the trypsin paralogs, suggesting a rapid process of functional diversification.
source: Moreover, we found very distinct patterns of transcript and protein abundance (measured by the number of unique peptides identified) across the trypsin paralogs (Figure 9B), suggesting a rapid process of functional diversification.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of expression and proteomic analysis with reference to figure and inference.

claim: Trypsins seem to be a recurrently used effector gene family in osmotrophic eukaryotes, and have evolved rapidly in Creolimax.
source: Thus, trypsins seem to be a recurrently used effector gene family in osmotrophic eukaryotes, and have evolved rapidly in Creolimax.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the comparative and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: 163 genes confidently branched within bacterial clades, supporting bacterial origins through LGT.
source: Manual inspection of these trees yielded a list of 163 genes that confidently branched within bacterial clades, supporting bacterial origins.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis.

claim: 35 LGT genes were found only in Creolimax among all eukaryotes sampled.
source: Of these, 35 (21.5%) were found only in Creolimax among all eukaryotes sampled, 50 (30.7%) were shared with the close relative Sphaeroforma arctica, and 71 (43.6%) were shared with other ichthyosporeans (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Most LGT genes (102 out of 163) were intron-less.
source: Although most LGT genes (102 out of 163) were intron-less, the vast majority (143, 87.7%) showed transcriptional support from our polyA-selected RNA-seq, minimizing the possibility of bacterial contaminations.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of structural and expression analysis.

claim: LGT from bacteria accounts for 1.8% of the total Creolimax proteome.
source: LGT from bacteria accounts for 1.8% of the total proteome, which is slightly higher than in other eukaryotic genomes (Alsmark et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of genome analysis with citation.

claim: 6 genes acquired by LGT were found in the in vivo secretome and 18 more in the in silico secretome.
source: Importantly, we found 6 genes acquired by LGT in the in vivo secretome and 18 more in the in silico secretome (Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of combined analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Ichthyosporeans have enriched their osmotrophy-related gene complement through prokaryotic LGT.
source: Therefore, similar to other eukaryotic lineages (Richards et al., 2011; Richards et al., 2011), ichthyosporeans have enriched their osmotrophy-related gene complement through prokaryotic LGT.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the LGT analysis with citations.

claim: Three of the six genes of prokaryotic origin found in the in vivo secretome belonged to the spore coat homology (CotH) family.
source: Among the six genes of prokaryotic origin that we found in the in vivo secretome, three belonged to the spore coat homology (CotH) family (PF08757).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of proteomic and domain analysis.

claim: CotH proteins were first described as being fundamental for spore coat formation in the bacteria Bacillus subtilis.
source: CotH proteins were first described as being fundamental for spore coat formation in the bacteria Bacillus subtilis (Naclerio et al., 1996), but they have recently been characterized as critical factors for host invasion in the fungus Rhizopus oryzae (Gebremariam et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated with citations to previous research.

claim: The presence of CotH homologs in Rhizopus oryzae and other fungi originated from an LGT event that was independent of those found in ichthyosporeans.
source: Our phylogenetic reconstruction of CotH family evolution revealed that the presence of CotH homologs in R. oryzae and other fungi (only belonging to the class mucorales) originated from an LGT event that was independent of those found in ichthyosporeans (Figure 10 and Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Both ichthyosporeans and mucorales have expanded their CotH family members after LGT acquisition.
source: Interestingly, both lineages have expanded their CotH family members after LGT acquisition.
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis.

claim: CotH genes were also found in other eukaryotic and archaeal lineages, suggesting a complex history of interdomain LGT.
source: Moreover, CotH genes were also found in other eukaryotic and archaeal lineages, suggesting a complex history of interdomain LGT similar to that recently described for other gene families (Funkhouser-Jones et al., 2014; Chou et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated directly as a result of phylogenetic analysis with citations and inference.

claim: Active transcription and secretion of Creolimax CotH genes in axenic culture conditions underscore their putative role in host invasion.
source: Active transcription and secretion of Creolimax CotH genes in axenic culture conditions underscore their putative role in host invasion and highlight the importance of LGT in effector gene acquisition across different osmotrophic lineages.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the expression and proteomic data.

claim: Creolimax employs complex gene regulation including alternative splicing and the use of long intergenic non-coding RNAs.
source: Here we describe the transcriptome dynamics of Creolimax fragrantissima, which has been proposed as a model system for ichthyosporeans (Suga and Ruiz-Trillo, 2013; Marshall et al., 2008). We show that Creolimax employs complex gene regulation including alternative splicing and the use of long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNA).
evidence: Stated directly as a main finding with citations.

claim: The study provides evidence of secondary adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode through lateral gene transfer (LGT) and gene duplication.
source: Through analysis of the Creolimax secretome in silico and by proteomics, we also provide evidence of secondary adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode through lateral gene transfer (LGT) and gene duplication.
evidence: Stated directly as a main finding.

claim: The results suggest that the last common unicellular ancestor of animals was already capable of implementing elaborate, cell type-specific differentiation programs.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that the last common unicellular ancestor of animals was already capable of implementing elaborate, cell type-specific differentiation programs.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: The unicellular amoeboid stage and not the multinucleate stage is defined by multicellularity-related activities in Creolimax.
source: Intriguingly, while this complex genome regulation in Creolimax often involves similar gene toolkits to those employed in animal development, it is the unicellular amoeboid stage and not the multinucleate stage that is defined by multicellularity-related activities.
evidence: Stated directly as a key observation from the study.

claim: The multinucleate stage of Creolimax can be regarded as a highly specialized proliferative cell type.
source: Thus, we consider that the multinucleate stage of Creolimax can be regarded as a highly specialized proliferative cell type.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The multinucleate stage can be considered to function in a manner analogous to stem cells, with the undifferentiated nuclei dividing before differentiation into amoeboid cells closes the lifecycle.
source: This cell type can be considered to function in a manner analogous to stem cells, with the undifferentiated nuclei dividing in the multinucleate cell before differentiation into amoeboid cells closes the lifecycle.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Separation of functions as crucial as self-renewal and differentiation can occur in a unicellular context in a temporal manner.
source: This would suggest that separation of functions as crucial as self-renewal and differentiation can occur in a unicellular context in a temporal manner, which pre-dates the exclusive ability of multicellular organisms to engulf both functionally distinct cell types within a single entity (Arendt, 2008; Hemmrich et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the data with citations.

claim: Creolimax has undergone secondary adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode, shaping its secretome and genome through both gene duplication and acquisition of bacterial genes by LGT.
source: For example, we show that Creolimax has undergone secondary adaptation to a specialized osmotrophic feeding mode, shaping its secretome and genome through both gene duplication and acquisition of bacterial genes by LGT.
evidence: Stated directly as a main finding.

claim: Many of the components of the animal genetic toolkit are assembled in co-regulated gene modules preserved since the common ancestor of all holozoans.
source: Moreover, many of the components of this toolkit are assembled in co-regulated gene modules preserved since the common ancestor of all holozoans, suggesting that recurrent recruitment of full co-regulated gene programs underlies the evolution of lineage-specific cell types and developmental modes (Newman, 2012).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the co-regulation analysis with citation.

claim: The diversity of cellular behaviors and morphologies observed in holozoan lifecycles is likely to have evolved from lineage-specific specializations.
source: We have shown that the diversity of cellular behaviors and morphologies observed in holozoan lifecycles is likely to have evolved from lineage-specific specializations.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the comparative analysis.

claim: The rise of animal multicellularity may be seen as a derived specialization involving the integration of ancestral molecular modules and their associated cell behaviors into one single multicellular entity.
source: Nevertheless, the rise of animal multicellularity is not directly homologous to any ancestral developmental mode, and it may be seen as another derived specialization involving the integration of ancestral molecular modules and their associated cell behaviors into one single multicellular entity.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the study's findings.

claim: The capacity to build differentiated cell types and transient multicellular entities was not a rare feature in pre-metazoan evolution.
source: Our data suggests a third mixed model, in which the capacity to build differentiated cell types and transient multicellular entities was not a rare feature in pre-metazoan evolution.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion based on the study's findings.
